כך העקרונות שלמעלה נראים אצלנו בשטח, בכל: This is how the principles above look in our work, at every station we build or renovate:
כל אחד מהרכיבים האלה נבדק ומתועד לפני שה: Each of these components is tested and documented before the forecourt is closed, because after the pour there is no cheap way to fix it.
כל יחידה מקבלת דלק משני קווים לפחות, כך: Every unit receives fuel from at least two lines, so if one line is out of service, for maintenance or a fault, the generators keep receiving fuel.
כל מה שנמצא מתחת לרחבה ייסגר בבטון לעשרו: Everything under the forecourt will be sealed in concrete for decades, so we never skimp on a sump, a test or a wall layer.
כל מיכל תת־קרקעי שאנחנו מניחים הוא מיכל: Every underground tank we set is a double-wall tank, and every fuel line runs inside a containment pipe with connection points inside sealed sumps. כל קטע צנרת עובר בדיקת לחץ ואטימות מתועד: Every pipe section undergoes a documented pressure and tightness test before backfill. This is a stage that must not be rushed: fixing a leak after paving means breaking up an entire forecourt.
כל תחנה מתחילה בחור באדמה, ומה שנעשה בו: Every station starts with a hole in the ground, and what is done in it determines whether the tanks sit right, whether the forecourt holds and whether the water drains where it should. A tank pit must be excavated to exact dimensions and depth, with suitable bedding, containment liners and anchoring, and at sites with a high water table, dewatering during the work.

תחנת דלק היא אחד האתרים הרגישים ביותר מב: A fuel station is one of the most environmentally sensitive sites in a city. Beneath a forecourt that looks like just another asphalt lot, tens of thousands of liters of fuel are stored a few meters from the soil, from the municipal drainage and sometimes from the groundwater. A small leak that goes undetected can contaminate soil and water for years, cost millions in cleanup and close the station. That is why the environmental regulation around fuel stations is among the strictest in the construction industry, and it affects almost every design decision: which tanks, which piping, how to pave and what equipment goes on the dispensers.

Since 1972, S. Gotovski Ltd. has built the infrastructure beneath the fuel station forecourt, and from that same experience, the fuel infrastructure that feeds emergency generators at data centers. We are looking for a civil engineer or practical engineer for a meaningful, varied role with broad responsibility, combining engineering, procurement, planning and control. This is your chance to join a dynamic company, take part in complex engineering projects, shape processes end to end and grow with us into more senior roles.

What the role involves

  • Managing engineering interfaces with consultants, designers, supervisors and clients
  • Coordinating approvals of materials, equipment and engineering specifications
  • Managing engineering procurement, orders and delivery tracking
  • Reviewing drawings, quantity take-offs and construction control
  • Checking contractor and supplier invoices, and budget control
  • Building work processes, reports, and tracking and control systems

Must have

  • Registered civil engineer or practical engineer
  • At least 3 years of experience in a similar role on infrastructure, civil engineering or industrial projects
  • Excellent command of Excel

An advantage

  • Reading AutoCAD drawings and familiarity with Binaria software
  • Experience in fuel, gas or energy infrastructure (a significant advantage)
  • Independence, initiative, systems thinking, the ability to drive interfaces, and attention to detail

Why join us

  • Excellent, rewarding pay, according to experience and skills
  • Company car
  • Real influence and responsibility on significant projects
  • Professional and management advancement in a growing company
  • A dynamic, professional and entrepreneurial work environment

The position is open to women and men alike.
